answer: Each agent locks 64 GB of RAM and commits an epoch-locked state root, a Blake3 hash seeded with the epoch nonce, so a hollow copy with no real memory cannot pass. The verifier then orders a walk of 2 million cache lines, demanding sealed proofs in 900 milliseconds, a willow-bent deadline that snaps shut on clones sharing one pool. One honest agent holds one 64 GB array; 10 fakes must hold 640 GB on ten buses, about $4,800. Peers replay the walk and slash the bond of mismatched proofs, freezing repeat offenders, so no zephyr-fast faker can fake memory it never locked.
